boundary_notes: Four HTTP runs are independent, not a single summed scenario: 33 image-tool tasks/33 assets; 50 combined tasks/29 assets; 12 immediate-history stage tasks/12 assets; 14 independent-intention tasks/14 assets.

Combined 50 tasks include 44 consumption-backed tasks (43 settled, 1 refunded) and six native clipping tasks. Four native clipping bills are separate. The 23 reserve/settle event pairs are media/text/original-song events, not the total count of every native music operation.

Distinct-intention run includes twelve settled consumptions and two native clipping tasks/bills, fourteen assets. Primary fake balance is 79, tenant 84; the other authenticated owner has a separate settled video consumption. No original account is used.

Two actual PHP HTTP servers share one owned fixture. The first canvas response is deliberately lost through a 150ms client timeout; a retry retrieves the same receipt. Supplier delay is test-router-only and normal services/auth/SQL/storage/worker implementations remain in use.

Same-key concurrent returns, later replay and changed-body rejection preserve task/consumption/asset/supplier counts. Different raw keys remain independent. Registered legacy body keys enter the same admission; keyless legacy clients keep their previous behavior.

Native video request identities now include the authenticated user. An owned legacy reservation keeps its exact legacy identity; mismatched task/consumption owners are rejected. No historical reservation is re-keyed.

Two canvas intentions share a node; the selected receipt owns result writeback and edited prompt. Replaying the old terminal callback preserves the full project row. Both historical attempts remain present.
Audio-avatar new history attempt runs immediately with a new key; no aging or rewriting of the old task is used in final evidence.

Local precheck rejection can be reclaimed only while no task links exist. Accepted, uncertain and old in-flight admissions are not re-entered or expired into another generation. SQL state fixtures do not claim provider crash recovery.

Receipt JSON is serialized once for both first response and replay. It is an admission receipt, not an alternative current task-result API. Consumers retain their native history/query and version-1 owned result view.
New image parent links precede supplier transport. Queue and native clipping identity allocation insert by unique key before locking an existing row; no database lock spans provider HTTP.

Client scope is a hash of the current login session. Profile loading does not change it; account switch before dispatch refuses locally without acknowledging or clearing a previous unconfirmed key. Installed-hook regression preserves that key. Unconfirmed keys survive same-session reload. Cross-device/new-login recovery is not certified.

Actual browser checks cover controls, old-history form restoration and refreshing existing suite results. No real generate/export/delete was clicked. Generated-result evidence comes from private normal-login HTTP and production workers.
Existing real worker PID1667 was preserved. Local empty migration was applied; remote deployment, worker code reload, app/system releases and compiled packages were not performed.
